quizzes.stem: Scenario: Cobalt Logistics has three proposals for a returns-handling service. One has no way to learn from wrong answers, one is a workflow and one is a team of agents. A board member wants the cheapest. What should the architect do first?

options.a: Reject the cheapest design if the board has not yet seen its performance figures on live data
options.b: Compare the three on the same four stages and drop any that lacks one of them
options.c: Ask each team to run its design on a hundred real returns and compare the token bills
options.d: Choose the workflow because workflows always cost less than an agent in every case

explanation.b: A review applies the same questions to every design, and the missing stage is the first finding.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a design with a missing stage is rejected first: "no prompt can fix" it, and live figures do not repair it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because price is compared only "among those that pass the review".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page prices a workflow at "one chat per step", so a long workflow can cost more than the rung above it.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Heron Analytics proposes a team of six agents to produce a weekly summary of one internal dashboard. The summary is worth about one chat's cost to the readers. What does the pattern rule say?

options.a: Use the team, since six agents finish the summary faster than any single agent could do alone
options.b: Use one agent with tools, since a team always loses on a task of limited scope
options.c: Leave it off that rung, since the benefit falls short of the price of any extra machinery
options.d: Split the dashboard into six sections so each agent has a slice of equal size to read

explanation.c: The value is below what an agent costs, so no rung of autonomy pays.
explanation.a: Ruled out because speed is not one of the three reasons, and a team needs "independence, volume and value together".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the same shortfall applies one rung down: "its value is below what even one agent costs".
explanation.d: Ruled out because splitting the work does not create value, and a task worth less than that "is not a candidate, however neat the decomposition".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: At Alder Freight an intake service and a pricing service each pass every one of their own tests. In production about one request in fifty stalls between them, and always for shipments with no matching tariff. What does this most likely indicate?

options.a: Upgrading the pricing service to a more capable model so it copes with unusual shipments
options.b: An unwritten rule for how the two parts treat a lookup that finds nothing
options.c: A transient network fault that an automatic retry would clear on the next attempt
options.d: A third component placed between the two that logs every request and response

explanation.b: Both parts pass their own checks, so the gap is what neither contract says about the empty case.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a bigger model "only changes how the same ambiguity is worded".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a failure that follows an input pattern "is deterministic, and a retry repeats it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because logging adds a component and not a rule, and the page says to "Find the case the contract left out".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Cobalt Freight's design has an input stage, a processing stage, a feedback loop and an output stage that writes the model's text straight into the shipping database with no check. What does the rubric report?

options.a: No finding, since all four stages are present in the design and the loop is in place
options.b: A high finding, so the verdict is reject whatever the price of the whole design
options.c: A medium finding, so the verdict is revise until a vetting step is added
options.d: A finding for the missing feedback stage, since nothing is ever learned from the results

explanation.c: A stage that exists but lets text through unchecked is a medium finding, and a medium finding gives `revise`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rubric raises a finding when "There is an output stage that has no validation step".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "any `high` gives `reject`, otherwise any `medium` gives `revise`", and nothing here is high.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the finding for that is raised when "There is no feedback stage", and this design has one.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Fenwick Bank's board compares three designs for an account-opening service and asks which to build. One lacks a feedback stage, one is a validated workflow and one is a team of agents with a cheaper estimate. What does the review say?

options.a: Reject the one missing its learning loop, then pick the least expensive of the remaining pair
options.b: Choose the team, because its lower estimate already reflects efficient parallel work
options.c: Choose the workflow, since workflows are always the most economical form of design
options.d: Approve all three, and use the live results to decide which should stay in service

explanation.a: The verdict follows the worst finding, and price decides only among designs that pass.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a lower estimate does not matter for a rejected design: "a cheaper design with a missing feedback loop is not cheaper".
explanation.c: Ruled out because no rung is cheapest everywhere, and a workflow "costs one chat per step".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the review "records a finding for each stage that is absent" before anything goes live.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Willow Bank's complaint triage design collects a rating from customers for every reply and stores the ratings in a table that nobody reads. How should the review treat the feedback stage?

options.a: As present, since a rating is collected for every reply that customers receive
options.b: As absent, since no path leads from those scores to a change in the system
options.c: As present, once the ratings table is backed up on a regular schedule
options.d: As absent only if the table holds fewer than a thousand rows of ratings

explanation.b: The stage is defined by "the path by which they change the system", and here there is none.
explanation.a: Ruled out because collecting a rating is logging and not a loop: the stage holds "Evaluation, logging, human corrections, and the path by which they change the system".
explanation.c: Ruled out because backups protect the table and do not change the system, and the cost of the gap is that "Nobody learns that it was wrong".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the size of a table does not decide the finding, and a pipeline that "never learns from the result" goes wrong whatever its volume.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Quince Retail runs a returns agent that writes refunds to the ledger without approval, and the auditors require a record of each approval. What does the rubric report?

options.a: A medium finding, because the missing approval can be added during later testing
options.b: No finding, since the agent's answers have already been validated before the write
options.c: A finding about autonomy, since the path of a return is known in advance
options.d: A high finding, which makes the verdict reject whatever the cost of the design

explanation.d: A write without approval where an audit is needed is a `high` finding, so the verdict is reject.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The verdict follows the worst finding", and the rubric names `high` for this one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule fires when "The design writes without approval and an audit is needed", whatever was validated.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that finding applies only when "An agent or a team is used on a path that is already known".
